# Mycelium 360 critique (third party, received 2026-11-12)

*Vendored as received from the maintainer: the reviewer's summary, then the reviewer's reply to the project's first response. The reviewer's full per-layer document was offered and has not been received. The reviewer states: "This is from six independent code readers plus my own reading of the philosophy and prior reviews. I confirmed each layer's lead finding against the code; nothing was built or run."*

> **Added by the project, not the reviewer** (2026-11-12, at the request of the independent review of #773). Part 2
> answers the project's first response, which was not kept as a document. Its plan, which Part 2 refers to by number (items 1, 2 and 5),
> was, from the maintainer's account:
>
> 1. guard the KV read routes;
> 2. owner-signed security records (the grant use marker, a signed and anchored audit head, `cap/`·`req/`·`prov-shed`);
> 3. one door function for authorization;
> 4. catalogue version and expiry;
> 5. the electorate mandatory for the exclusive verbs, and a model of the acceptor;
> 6. `#[non_exhaustive]` on `GossipConfig`, with a constructor.
>
> Everything outside this block is the critique as received, unchanged.

## Part 1 — the summary

**Verdict:** the low-level engineering is disciplined, but the trust model and breadth are the problem. Almost every guarantee above Layer II holds against a gateway client and fails against one compromised or buggy mesh member. The project is also far wider than one person can keep correct.

Several findings are limits the threat model already states, but they still undercut the headline claims.

### The one root cause

"Detection, not prevention" at Layer I, combined with a flat fleet-CA trust model, means any member can write any key. The upper layers then store their security state in that same KV:

- Grants: the used-marker is a gossip key; a member can tombstone it to re-arm a grant, and two gateways can admit the same grant concurrently.
- Audit: the chain lives in gossip KV with no signed head or external anchor, so tail truncation is undetectable.
- Provisioning: cap/, req/ and prov-shed/ entries are unauthenticated, so one member can trigger installs, suppress healing or attract calls.
- Caller identity: a caller envelope is trusted if signed by any key of the sending node, so any member can assert any principal or scope.

The fix does not require teaching Layer I a law. Make security-bearing records owner-signed and verified at read, which is the pattern already used for sys/identity-cert/.

### Layer by layer

| Layer | Sound | Most serious problems |
|---|---|---|
| I — KV | Snapshot ordering, bounded decoding, very few panics | Anti-entropy applies unsigned entries with unbounded timestamps, so a u64::MAX stamp pins a key forever (mycelium-core/src/connection.rs:843-868). Deleted keys can resurrect after about 50 minutes. No checksum on WAL records. SWIM is unauthenticated UDP even under TLS. |
| II — Signals | Bounded queues, good papaya discipline | Signal frames are unsigned and readable by every relay (mycelium-core/src/framing.rs:193-204), so RPC replies are forgeable and mandates travel in clear past hop TLS. Quorum-evidence writes amplify each signal by N. Nonce is marked seen before validation. |
| III — Consensus | Fsync-before-reply, pure tested decision functions, no panics | Default quorum is sized from the local live-peer view, so a 3\|2 partition can commit two lock holders (src/agent/consensus_handle.rs:336). No model or linearizability checker exists. Leases have no skew margin and nothing checks the fencing token. |
| IV — Capabilities | No shell injection path, WASI deny-by-default, confinement fails closed when declared | Catalogue signatures carry no version or expiry, so any member can roll the fleet back (mycelium-wasm-host/src/catalog.rs:154-168). Native activation is unconfined unless declared. Stems stage blobs before checking provenance. |
| V — Gateway/authority | Authentication is one layer; constant-time tokens; TLS resumption off | Everything after authentication is by convention: protected kinds are checked by hand at 9 sites, preflight at about 10. Raw KV reads have no namespace guard (src/agent/http/kv.rs:13-25), so kv:read reads grants and audit. Default TLS keeps the CA key on every node. |

### Philosophy: what I would keep and change

Keep:
- Coordinator-free and embedded.
- Receipts that name their rung (Property 9), the project's best idea.
- Litmus tests 4 and 5.
- The "what is proven" page.

Change:

1. Signals and Boundaries is no longer what ships. With group_aware_forwarding on by default, Individual frames go direct when a route exists and Group frames go to members plus three random peers. That is the right engineering, so restate the principle as "flood to discover and broadcast, route what is addressed". Then add what the Holland framing hides: signed signals and end-to-end encryption for Individual scope. A boundary today is a courtesy filter, not isolation.
2. "Consensus is a protocol the substrate is unaware of" has a real cost. It leaves consensus with no authoritative membership, which is the split-brain above. Electorates then rebuild Raft's configuration log in about 3k lines of the hardest code in the repo, unmodelled. Make the electorate mandatory for lock/, leader/ and consistent/, and write a Stateright or TLA+ model of the acceptor, slot reuse and migration. Had the goal been only locks and leaders on a declared voter set, openraft would have been the better choice.
3. "Detection, not prevention" is right for availability and wrong as a security posture. Keep it for Layer I; stop relying on it for grants, audit and provisioning.
4. "Library, not platform" no longer describes the product. There is a published node binary, a stem, doctor, init, declare, a gateway with 86 routes and two SDKs that reach it as a sidecar. Either own the platform shape or cut back to the library.
5. The philosophy document argues by analogy. Hayek, Ostrom, Bookchin and Rojava carry no engineering weight, and they make it easier to defend a design choice by lineage than by measurement. I would cut it to Holland, Promise Theory, the litmus tests and Properties 8 and 9.
6. Defaults. A dev-posture default is defensible for a library, but "token set" reads as "secured" when no evaluator, provider enforcement or journal is attached. Warn at start, and make self-install opt-in, not the headline default.

### Language choice

Rust is the right choice for Layers I–III and I would not rewrite. Its costs here are self-inflicted:

- Feature flags: 2,253 cfg(feature) lines, 11 clippy invocations, and two extra crates that exist only to test feature-off builds. Make consensus unconditional and move the gateway to its own crate.
- API churn: 98 deprecation sections and struct-literal breaks in MINOR releases. GossipConfig has 84 public fields and is not #[non_exhaustive].
- Audience mismatch: the target users write Python and TypeScript, so for them "embedded" means a sidecar. The SDKs are hand-written against no OpenAPI schema.

### Code areas needing attention, in order

1. Authorization path (src/agent/http/authz.rs, src/agent/gateway_caller.rs, src/agent/action_evaluator.rs): replace hand-called checks with a typed Authorized<Scope> extractor and one door function that owns preflight, dispatch, release and record. This is why "door X skipped door Y's check" keeps recurring.
2. src/consensus.rs (5.5k lines, propose_inner 414): split into state-machine steps and model-check it.
3. Four separate append-log implementations (core WAL, src/agent/journal.rs, tuple-space, blackboard): extract one checksummed log and crash-test it once.
4. handle_connection, a single 929-line function in mycelium-core/src/connection.rs.
5. TaskCtx in src/agent/mod.rs: 90 fields and 59 cfg attributes, the cause of 56 too_many_arguments allows.
6. Catalogue metadata: add version, expiry and revocation (TUF-style), and verify provenance before staging.
7. src/lib_tests.rs: 18k lines in one file, about 650 fixed sleeps in tests, and a retry wrapper referenced 30 times in CI.
8. Comments: roughly 15–20% narrate review history ("#708's review, round 2") instead of stating the invariant; several are stale.

## Part 2 — the reviewer's reply to the project's first response

**Where they are right**

- The headline was too strong after v2.40.0. A member can no longer forge a certificate holder's call signature (I1), a signed grant decision (I3) or an OIDC user's token (I5). "Almost every guarantee fails against one member" should read "the guarantees whose state is an unsigned KV record fail against one member". That is the narrower list they give: re-arming a use marker, asserting a keyless principal, writing cap/ entries, truncating the audit chain.
- consensus.rs is 6,503 lines. The 5.5k was production lines with test blocks excluded, and I dropped the qualifier.
- Routes: 76 in the main router (src/agent/http/mod.rs). The 86 was every .route( registration including companion routers; 76 is the better number for the gateway.
- openraft is a counterfactual. The actionable part is the model, and I'm glad they'd take it.

**Where I hold**

- Two of the v2.40.0 protections are conditional, and the pushback states them as absolute.
  - The exchanged token is required for an oidc: principal only where the provider sets exchange_audience; otherwise the check returns Ok(None) (src/agent/gateway_caller.rs:1348-1353).
  - An unsigned call for a certificate holder is counted, not refused (src/agent/gateway_caller.rs:1405-1409). This is the plan's O-series: counters that become refusals a release later.

  So "a member can't" is true today only on a provider configured for it. The upgrade notes should say so until the refusals land.
- "The secure profile refuses it" answers the profile, not the default. The split-brain needs a fleet with no electorate, and that is what GossipConfig::default() gives. distributed_lock there returns success from a minority partition. I would make the exclusive verbs refuse without an electorate in every profile; they have that at item 5, so we agree on the fix.
- The philosophy cut is more than taste in one respect. Trimming the lineage is the author's call. The Signals and Boundaries mismatch is not: the document says forwarding is unconditional, and the shipped default routes Individual frames directly and samples Group fan-out. The project's own rule is that a document must not claim more than the code does.
- "A library that also ships a reference node" is a fair wording and I would accept it. It still leaves Python and TypeScript users on a sidecar, which the positioning should say plainly.

**On their plan**

The order is right. Three additions:

1. Do item 1 today. The KV read guard is a small, self-contained fix for a live hole (kv:read reads grant/ and sys/audit/). It should not wait for a verification pass.
2. Write item 2 as a rule. Three rediscoveries in one week is the evidence. Wave 1b's I4 and I2 will each add records of this kind, so the rule should exist before they are built, or it will be rediscovered a fourth and fifth time.
3. Add two cheap Layer I items they did not list: refuse an inbound entry stamped beyond the drift bound, and add a checksum per WAL record. Neither needs a wire change.
